subsystems.name: Delivery drone
subsystems.role: carries the package and flies the route.

subsystems.name: Mesh communication
subsystems.role: lets drones talk to each other and to ground nodes without relying on a central tower.

subsystems.name: Edge autonomy
subsystems.role: computes flight paths, collision avoidance and coordination onboard in real time.

subsystems.name: Navigation
subsystems.role: keeps the drone on course and aware of its position.

subsystems.name: Ground infrastructure
subsystems.role: supports take-off, landing, charging and package handover.

subsystems.name: Traffic management
subsystems.role: integrates drones into airspace and prevents conflicts with other aircraft.

buildSteps.title: Design airframe and payload
buildSteps.detail: Choose a multirotor for hover-and-deliver or a fixed-wing VTOL for longer range; size the battery for the required payload and distance.

buildSteps.title: Integrate flight controller and sensors
buildSteps.detail: Install the autopilot, GNSS, inertial measurement unit and obstacle-detection sensors, then tune for stable flight.

buildSteps.title: Develop mesh networking
buildSteps.detail: Write the protocol for drone-to-drone and drone-to-ground communication, including routing and handover between moving nodes.

buildSteps.title: Implement edge computing
buildSteps.detail: Program onboard computers to run path planning, collision avoidance and swarm-coordination algorithms without a central server.

buildSteps.title: Build ground stations
buildSteps.detail: Set up landing pads, charging or battery-swap stations and mesh gateways across the service area.

buildSteps.title: Simulate and flight-test
buildSteps.detail: Use software simulation and controlled flights to validate coordination, safety and failure modes.

buildSteps.title: Certify and integrate with traffic management
buildSteps.detail: Obtain regulatory approval for beyond-visual-line-of-sight operations and connect to airspace-management systems.

prerequisites.why: current lithium-ion packs limit range and payload; better cells are needed for practical delivery distances.
drones must reliably sense and avoid other aircraft and obstacles without a human pilot.
regulators need a way to track and separate many drones in shared airspace.
decentralised communication between fast-moving nodes is not yet standardised for aviation use.
powerful, low-power processors are available for onboard autonomy and real-time routing.

pathway.milestone: pilot projects delivering medical supplies and small parcels in limited areas
pathway.unlocks: real-world data on range, reliability and public acceptance.

pathway.milestone: routine beyond-visual-line-of-sight operations in selected corridors
pathway.unlocks: remote supervision of many drones instead of one pilot per aircraft.

pathway.milestone: urban mesh networks where drones coordinate routes directly with each other
pathway.unlocks: denser delivery without a single point of failure or central bottleneck.

pathway.milestone: fully autonomous mesh logistics integrated with ground robots and airspace management
pathway.unlocks: same-hour delivery at city scale as a normal utility.
